cover_letter:
Dear Whale team,

I'm writing to apply for the AI Creative Specialist position. Your description of shipping with the latest models from day one, turning one idea into fifty variants by lunch, and building a prompt library that compounds speed—that's the way I already work. I use LLMs like Claude and ChatGPT daily for research, content and audits, and I've built prompt workflows that let me generate and test many creative directions quickly. While my title has been in SEO and web, the core is the same: use AI and code to automate the repetitive, so I can focus on what looks right and what performs.

In my freelance work, I designed and built baverok.com and mirook.com, handling everything from structure to content to technical implementation. I've also used AI tools to automate SEO audits and content production, and I've developed an Android app that's live on Google Play—proof that I can take an idea from concept to shipped product. At Episto, I manage content for client sites and use data to refine what works. I don't just adopt new tools; I integrate them into workflows that scale.

What draws me to Whale is the emphasis on real ownership and speed. I thrive when I can ship, get feedback, and ship again. I have a strong sense of taste—I know when something looks right, not just done—and I'm eager to push boundaries with every new model that drops. I'm confident I can contribute creative that drives campaigns from week one.

I'd welcome the chance to discuss how my mix of AI fluency, creative instinct, and technical execution can help Whale scale its creative output. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Baver Ok
